children: HDFC Bank share price rose over 1% on September 21, with the stock hitting Rs 738.55 as Indian equities traded higher

Shares of HDFC Bank rose more than 1 per cent on September 21, touching a day’s high of Rs 738.55 as the private sector lender gained alongside a firmer domestic equity market. The stock was trading around Rs 738.55 at midday, up about 1.04 per cent from its previous close of Rs 729.10. The rise came as benchmark Indian equities also moved higher during the session.

HDFC Bank remained among the key large-cap stocks supporting the broader market. Reuters reported that Indian equities were trading higher on Monday, with the Nifty 50 and Sensex gaining during mid-morning trade amid buying in select heavyweight stocks.

HDFC Bank had closed at Rs 729.10 on September 18, after gaining 2.26 per cent during the previous session. The stock opened at Rs 731 on September 21 and moved within a range of around Rs 729 to Rs 738 during the trading session. The stock has remained under focus amid the bank’s ongoing management succession process.

HDFC Bank had earlier submitted names of candidates to the Reserve Bank of India for the position of managing director and chief executive officer, as current CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan is set to step down later this year.
At the September 21 intraday level, HDFC Bank’s market capitalisation was around Rs 11.4 lakh crore. The stock remained below its 52-week high of around Rs 1,020, according to market data.

The movement in HDFC Bank shares also came against a mixed global backdrop, with investors tracking crude oil prices, bond yields and geopolitical developments. Brent crude eased on Monday after recent gains, while global markets remained sensitive to developments in the Middle East and expectations around US monetary policy.
